_comment: LIVE page inventory for every Figma file the catalog tracks, harvested directly
from Figma rather than from figma.txt. This exists because the catalog's node lists are
parsed from that hand-maintained link dump, so any page never pasted into it is
structurally invisible - the root cause of every coverage gap found on 2026-07-28.
build-registry.mjs reads this to stamp `page` and `readiness` on every frame and to
REPORT pages that no section covers, so the next missing page announces itself.
readiness comes from the leading emoji of the page NAME, which is the convention the
team actually uses (Casey, 2026-07-28). Figma's real Dev Mode devStatus flag is not
readable here: the MCP plugin sandbox rejects the getter and get_metadata omits it.
liveChildren = count of TOP-LEVEL children on the page, including furniture
(Directory / Breakpoint / Rectangle N / Vector N), so it is NOT directly comparable
to a section's frame count. null means not counted. Counting REQUIRES
setCurrentPageAsync per page: an unloaded page reports children.length === 0 rather
than throwing, so a bulk read silently reports an empty file. Every count below was
taken with an explicit page switch.

This matters beyond tidiness. figma-drift.mjs joins a REMOVED old id to an
ADDED new id by EXACT TITLE to recognise a rebuild (RETARGET). That join reads
the title from the REGISTRY on one side and from LIVE FIGMA on the other, so a
registry title that no longer equals the live name silently disables the
rescue for that frame — it would report as REMOVED and its implFiles would
look orphaned. Leaving a stale title in place is therefore not the safe
option; it is the failure mode. The rule that protects the join is 'the
registry title must equal the live Figma name', which is why titles are
re-harvested from <section>.titles.tsv on every build and are NOT in
build-registry's preserved-hand-set list. What must never happen is a
hand-authored 'more accurate' title that matches neither.

figma-drift.social-0821.json, so no prior name is lost by this update.

The tombstone pages in Skai-Web-App carry node ids 2003:674 / 2998:19593 / 3:3 - the SAME ids as Home 1 / Wallet 1 / Trade 1 in Skai-Web-App-2. Their text reads "moved to Skai Web App 2", which names the FILE. Home 1 IS the moved page.
